correctness.rationale: For all positive n, Beatty complementarity yields the exact sum over k≤floor(delta n). The membership floor increment becomes an indicator H_y of at most two intervals under golden rotation. Fibonacci-denominator discrepancy O(log n) uniformly in phase plus its direct interval integral proves r(n)=nF({delta n})+O(log n). Irrational equidistribution pushes the three-piece profile to the atom-plus-flat density. Lipschitz transport estimate and bounded variation give W1=O(log² X/X). Exact integer pair convolution and independent phase-count checks via verify.py confirmed n≤4500, not used to certify the infinite claims.

originality.rationale: Full primary-text comparison: Ashburn arXiv:2610.04842v1 proves exactly 0/1/2 representations; Shallit arXiv:2006.04177v1 §11.2 does give a rank-19 automatic linear representation for the same full counting function, but no phase-resolved uniform asymptotic, atom-plus-flat component, or quantitative Wasserstein law. OEIS A259598 lists the sequence and exceptional terms. Pongsriiam 2022 abstract covers cofinite sumsets. Searches across a semantic research index and open scholarly web did not locate an equivalent limiting law, but priority risks from general additive Beatty theory and matrix asymptotics remain.
residual_risks: Shallit 2020 already provides a full exact finite-state linear representation for the function; the limit law may be obtainable as a nontrivial but unrecorded consequence of that known encoding.
A previously published general theorem for convolution of Beatty sequences might directly imply this particular golden-ratio phase profile; absence from search results is not proof of uniqueness.
The complete text of the Pongsriiam 2022 and Kawsumarng et al. 2021 papers was not inspected, though their accessible abstracts and cited theorems were compared.
No independent external expert/priority review was performed.

value.rationale: The exact mixed Wythoff multiplicity function is a natural named object (OEIS A259598) recently studied for small representation counts. Its all-index phase-resolved normalized law reveals a positive-mass atom at the maximal linear-scale value and a precisely flat continuous component, plus an effective W1 rate. This is a substantive distributional structural result distinct from the previously known zero/one/two exceptions and finite-state exact representation; no downstream theorem needed.
